title: Kairos Power raises $643M to build nuclear reactors for Google
key_facts: Kairos Power raised $643 million in private and government financing for its demonstration reactor in Tennessee, Bloomberg reported.
$368 million came from investors including Google Ventures and DCVC; $275 million came from the US Energy Department.
$70 million of the private money came from Samsung C&T through a partnership announced in September.
The reactor, Hermes 2, is 50 megawatts and uses molten salt as a coolant instead of water; start-up is expected in 2030.
Kairos agreed last year to sell its power to the Tennessee Valley Authority for data centers owned by Google's parent Alphabet.
Some funds go to expanding manufacturing in New Mexico.
quote_evidence: Kairos Power LLC secured $643 million in combined private and government financing that will be utilized to support construction of its demonstration reactor in Tennessee.
Kairos expects its 50-megawatt Hermes 2 demonstration system in Tennessee to start up in 2030.
why_it_matters_hint: Tech companies' power demand is financing new kinds of nuclear reactors, though this one is years from running.
